title: OpenAI plans to revive AI video model Sora months after scrapping it: Report
source_used: The Information (AI Agenda newsletter, free opening, 12 Oct 2026), read with Digit, PYMNTS and ForkLog; the pool copy (Inshorts) is a two-sentence blurb of Digit
key_facts: The Information reported on 12 Oct 2026, citing a person with knowledge of the talks, that OpenAI is in talks with a stealthy startup developing AI video for filmmakers, which wants access to Sora to tweak it and sell software or other services using it.

The startup was co-founded in recent months by Hollywood producer Jeffrey Katzenberg, former Sora research lead Bill Peebles and former Dropbox chief financial officer Sujay Jaswa; its name is not known.

It is unclear whether the startup would be given Sora's weights (the settings that shape how the model responds); if the deal proceeds it would still get enough access to substantially customise the model.
The Information notes AI developers usually guard weights closely, but sharing them would not be surprising because Peebles knows how the model works.
The Information says OpenAI cancelled both the Sora model and its TikTok-like app earlier this year as part of a cull of server-intensive side projects.
Digit reads the talks as possibly bringing Sora back mainly as a tool for professional filmmakers rather than a service for everyone.
Outlets disagree on the closure date: Digit and ForkLog place the discontinuation announcement in March 2026 (ForkLog: 24 March), while the Inshorts blurb says April 2026.
ForkLog alone adds that OpenAI would receive a stake in the startup if the deal goes through; this is not in the other coverage read.
quote_evidence: A stealthy startup developing AI video for filmmakers, which we revealed last month, is in talks with OpenAI to access Sora, tweak it and sell software or other services using it, according to a person with knowledge of the talks.
Also unclear is whether this startup will be given access to Sora’s weights, or the settings that shape how the model responds to queries, The Information added.
If the deal goes ahead, the startup is expected to receive enough access to make significant changes to the model for its needs.
why_it_matters_hint: A shelved video model may come back as a professional tool for film, possibly out of reach for ordinary users.
notes: The pool copy is an Inshorts blurb that relays Digit, which relays The Information, so the credit goes to The Information. Read The Information's free opening, then Digit, PYMNTS and ForkLog in full. Single unnamed source; talks unconfirmed by OpenAI in the coverage read.
